newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Britain agree on HK satellite TV licence.
newsitem.headline: China, Britain agree on HK satellite TV licence.

text.p: China and Britain on Thursday reached agreement on a Hong Kong satellite television licence that straddles the British colony's return to Beijing rule in 1997, Chinese and British officials said.
The officials said in a joint statement that the two sides had signed what they described as an "agreed minute" on the satellite television licence.
The satellite licence for Galaxy television was one of a number of handover issues being discussed in Beijing by Chinese and British negotiators.
Hong Kong in 1994 granted Galaxy Uplink Ltd, a unit of local television broadcaster TVB, a 12-year licence to establish transmission and reception facilities in the British colony.
Beijing's approval was also needed because the deal straddled Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule next year.

British officials, speaking to reporters in Beijing, gave no further details of the television licence, but said there were now no "long-outstanding" contracts or franchises on the agenda of the Joint Liason Group (JLG).
The JLG was set up by China and Britain to handle issues that relate to Hong Kong's July 1, 1997 handover.
